title: Subarray Sum Equals K
prompt:
Given an array of integers nums and an integer k, return how many contiguous subarrays (non-empty stretches of consecutive elements) add up to exactly k.

Write subarraySum(nums, k).

  • subarraySum([20, 35, 0, 15, 40], 55) → 4 ([20,35], [20,35,0], [0,15,40], [15,40])
  • subarraySum([1, 1, 1], 2) → 2
  • subarraySum([1, -1, 0], 0) → 3 ([1,-1], [1,-1,0], [0])

Constraints: 0 <= nums.length <= 2 * 10^4, values may be negative, so a sliding window will not work. The O(n²) "every start, every end" loop is too slow; aim for O(n).

tests.name: negative numbers and zero (a sliding window would fail here)
subarrays starting at index 0 are counted
empty input and a single element
all zeros with k = 0 counts every subarray
agrees with brute force on a mixed array

hints: Trigger: count contiguous subarrays with sum k, and the numbers can be negative. That points to prefix sums plus a hash map, not a sliding window.

Idea: sum(start..end) = total after end − total before start. You want that to equal k, so at each position count how many earlier running totals equal runningTotal - k. Store counts of running totals in a Map, starting with {0: 1} for the empty prefix.

Code shape: const seen = new Map([[0, 1]]); let total = 0, count = 0; for (const x of nums) { total += x; count += seen.get(total - k) || 0; seen.set(total, (seen.get(total) || 0) + 1); }. Look up before you record the current total.
explain:
Time O(n), space O(n). One pass; each step does one map lookup and one map update. The brute force was O(n²) because, for every end position, it effectively re-scanned every start; the map remembers every earlier running total so that scan becomes one lookup.

This is Two Sum played on running totals: "find an earlier value equal to current − k". The same shape solves "subarray sum divisible by k" (store totals mod k) and "longest subarray with sum k" (store the first index of each total instead of a count).

How to say it: "A subarray sum is a difference of two prefix sums. I scan once, and for each running total I add how many times total − k appeared before, using a hash map seeded with {0: 1}. O(n) time and space, and it handles negatives, which a sliding window can't."
